title: Visual Anything view file
description: The contents of a `.vaview` file: a projection of the model onto the canvas, with its own positions.

nestingRelationTypes.description: The nesting relation types that arrange this view.

positions.description: The positions of anchored shapes, set by layout or pinned by hand. A shape without a position is placed by layout.

stackingOrder.description: The order in which this view draws the anchored shapes that sit directly inside each container, or directly in World, by the id of the container, or World's id. Each list goes from back to front: the shapes it does not name are drawn in front of the ones it names, in model order, so without a list every shape there is drawn in model order and a new shape comes in front. Every copy of a container draws its contents in the same order. An id whose element does not sit there is ignored.

collapsed.description: The containers this view shows collapsed, by element id, sorted. A collapsed container's shapes show none of its contents, and the relations to and from them are drawn as aggregated relations. An id that is no element of the model is ignored.

routes.description: The relations this view routes by hand, by relation id, each with only what differs from its automatic route: where its ends attach, the points it bends at, and its style. A relation it does not name is routed automatically, and a route whose relation is no relation of the model is ignored.

scope.description: The part of the model this view shows (ADR 0040). Without it, the view shows the whole model.

relationTypesLeftOut.description: The relation types whose relations this view does not draw (ADR 0064): not as lines, not in a collapsed container's aggregated relations, and in no count of relations that leave the view. Such a relation stays in the model. A relation type the view nests by draws containment, so it is never left out. Left out when it has none.

routeStyle.description: How this view draws the automatic routes of the relations whose appearances set no route (ADR 0069). Left out, they are orthogonal.

rows.description: Which rows the shapes that draw their contents as rows draw in this view (ADR 0080, section 5): every row, as when left out, or only their key rows, those whose element is part of a primary key or that a relation the view draws ends on, with a count of the rest.

selectionFadesLines.description: Whether selecting a shape or a relation, in a view with more than 40 lines, draws the lines that do not touch the selection faintly (ADR 0080, section 5). Left out, it does; `false` turns it off.

overlays.description: How this view colors, sizes, marks or fades its shapes by their attributes, in order (ADR 0055): each channel of a shape is set by the first overlay that sets it. Left out when it has none.

drawing.description: How this view draws what no appearance sets, changing the project's drawing defaults for it alone (ADR 0086). Left out, the project's.

conflicts.description: What a merge could not join, as data (ADR 0072): each conflict says which item it is about, what the file keeps in place, and the other choice. Written only by a merge; the person resolves them.

Id.description: An identifier, generated once and never reused. Files refer to each other only by id. Element and relation ids share one namespace, because a relation can end on either. Component and relation type ids start with their package's id, as in `systems.service`.

Perspective.description: The criterion for selecting and arranging the model in a view.

container.description: The container whose shape holds this one. Absent when the element sits directly in World.

x.description: The left edge, relative to the container's shape, or to the canvas when directly in World.

y.description: The top edge, relative to the container's shape, or to the canvas when directly in World.

pinned.description: Whether the position was set by hand. Layout arranges every other shape around pinned shapes.

rotation.description: How far the shape is turned clockwise about its middle, in degrees (ADR 0088). Its name stays level; containers drawn as regions and rows are never turned.

flip.description: Whether the shape's outline and image are mirrored (ADR 0088). Its name is never mirrored.

ShapePosition.description: Where an anchored shape sits in a view. An element has one anchored shape inside each of its containers, so a position is identified by the element and the container its shape sits in.

FreeShape.description: A shape that is drawing only and does not exist in the model.

x.description: Its left edge on the canvas.

y.description: Its top edge on the canvas.

fill.description: Its fill; without one, the theme's note color.

stroke.description: Its stroke; without one, the theme's.

Note.description: A free shape that holds text.

Color.description: A color written as `#RRGGBB`: no alpha, no short form and no names. Files may write the digits in either case; the program writes new colors in capitals and keeps a color's spelling when it is set to the same color again.

stroke.description: Its color; without one, the theme's arrow color.

Arrow.description: A free shape that points from one place on the canvas to another.

Point.description: A point on the canvas, in canvas units, at most ten million from its origin either way.

x.description: Its left edge on the canvas.

y.description: Its top edge on the canvas.

media.description: The media file it shows: an image, or a video (ADR 0098, stage 2).

poster.description: A video's poster: its first frame, kept as a PNG, JPEG or WebP media file when it is added, which it shows until it plays. Only a video has one, and one Claude adds has none.

name.description: What screen readers and the outline say, and what a missing file shows; "Picture", or "Video" for a video, when left out.

Picture.description: A free shape that shows a media file kept beside the project (ADR 0098): a photo, a screenshot, an animated GIF or an SVG drawing. It belongs to the view and is never part of the model.

hash.description: The SHA-256 of the cleaned file, in lowercase hexadecimal.

bytes.description: The size of the cleaned file, in bytes: an image's at most 32 MiB, a video's at most 50 MiB.

MediaRef.description: Which media file a picture shows and what it is, so that the scene can place it and an export can name it before the file is read (ADR 0098). The file is `media/<hash>.<extension>` beside the project.

MediaFormat.description: The formats a media file may have (ADR 0098): images, and from stage 2 videos, MP4 and WebM.

propertyNames.description: An identifier, generated once and never reused. Files refer to each other only by id. Element and relation ids share one namespace, because a relation can end on either. Component and relation type ids start with their package's id, as in `systems.service`.

StackingOrder.description: Stacking lists by the id of the container whose contents they order, or World's id for the shapes directly in World.

StackingList.description: Element ids, from back to front.

propertyNames.description: An identifier, generated once and never reused. Files refer to each other only by id. Element and relation ids share one namespace, because a relation can end on either. Component and relation type ids start with their package's id, as in `systems.service`.

Routes.description: Routes chosen by hand, by the id of the relation each one routes.

from.description: Where the line attaches to the relation's `from` end. An end that is a relation takes none: the line attaches to the middle of that relation's line.

to.description: Where the line attaches to the relation's `to` end.

style.description: `orthogonal` runs with square corners, `straight` straight from point to point and `curved` a smooth curve through them; left out, the route takes its automatic style (ADR 0069).

container.description: The container whose shape the bend points are relative to: one that holds the shapes of both ends, the nearest when they were set. Left out, they are relative to the canvas. While its shape no longer holds both ends, the bend points are ignored, and they come back with the containment.

bendPoints.description: The points the line passes through, in order from its `from` end, in canvas units, relative to the shape of `container`, or to the canvas.

RelationRoute.description: How a view routes one relation by hand: only what differs from its automatic route. An end left out attaches where the automatic route attaches it, a route without bend points runs directly between its ends, and one without a style is orthogonal.

EndAttachment.description: Where a line attaches to one of its ends, chosen by hand: one of the end's connection points, by name, a fixed place on its border, or a fixed place inside it.

name.description: The name of one of the connection points of the end's appearance.

ConnectionPointAttachment.description: The line attaches at one of the end's connection points, wherever the end's appearance puts it.

at.description: Where it sits along its side, from 0 at the side's left or top end to 1 at its right or bottom end.

BorderAttachment.description: The line attaches at a fixed place on the end's border, which follows the shape as it moves and resizes.

InsideAttachment.description: The line attaches at a fixed place inside the end's shape, anywhere on it, which follows the shape as it moves and resizes: across and down its box, each from 0 at its left or top to 1 at its right or bottom.

RouteStyle.description: How a line runs between its ends: square corners, straight, or a smooth curve.

added.description: Elements shown whatever the rules say: ids, sorted, each once, none of them in `leftOut`.

leftOut.description: Elements left out whatever the rules say: ids, sorted, each once, none of them in `added`.

Scope.description: The part of the model a view shows: the elements that meet one of its `include` rules, or every element when it has none, and none of its `exclude` rules; then those it adds, less those it leaves out. World always shows, and a relation shows while both its ends do.

ScopeRule.description: A rule of a scope: which elements it takes.

ComponentRule.description: The elements created from a component, and from every component derived from it unless `exactly`.

RelationTypeRule.description: The elements at either end of a relation of a relation type, or of one derived from it unless `exactly`.

ContentsRule.description: A container and what sits inside it through the view's nesting relation types: `depth` levels down, or every level without it.

value.description: What the value is compared with; left out for `set` and `unset`.

AttributeRule.description: The elements whose attribute meets a test, as filters test it, with its component's default when unset.

RelationTypesLeftOut.description: The relation types a view leaves out (ADR 0064), sorted by relation type, each once.

RelationTypeLeftOut.description: A relation type a view leaves out, with every relation type derived from it unless `exactly`.

Overlay.description: A rule of a view that colors, sizes, marks or fades its shapes by one attribute, which its legend explains (ADR 0055). It maps the attribute to one channel.

name.description: What the legend calls it; without one, the attribute's name.

of.description: Whether it reads the attributes of elements and changes their shapes, or of relations and changes their lines.

attribute.description: The attribute it reads: an element's or relation's own value, or the default its component or relation type gives.

off.description: Whether it is turned off: kept in the view, it changes nothing and its legend is left out.

FillOverlay.description: Fills shapes with a color by the attribute; relations have no fill.

ColorMapping.description: How an overlay of fill or stroke colors what it changes.

otherwise.description: The color of any value no case names; left out, such a shape keeps its own.

ColorCases.description: Values to colors, and the color of any other value, a missing one included.

CaseValue.description: A value an overlay compares an attribute with, as filters compare: text without minding case or the spaces around it, and numbers as numbers, so that "12" names 12 and "true" names true.

LegendLabel.description: What the legend says for a value or a stop; without it, the value.

stops.description: In increasing order of `at`, each at a number of its own.

ColorRamp.description: Numbers to colors along a ramp: up to the first stop its color, from the last its color, and between two stops their colors mixed. A value that is no number keeps its own.

ColorStop.description: A number and its color on a ramp.

Passthrough.description: The value is what the channel takes: a color written as #RRGGBB, or a badge's text.

name.description: What the legend calls it; without one, the attribute's name.

of.description: Whether it reads the attributes of elements and changes their shapes, or of relations and changes their lines.

attribute.description: The attribute it reads: an element's or relation's own value, or the default its component or relation type gives.

off.description: Whether it is turned off: kept in the view, it changes nothing and its legend is left out.

StrokeOverlay.description: Strokes shapes, or relations' lines, with a color by the attribute.

name.description: What the legend calls it; without one, the attribute's name.

of.description: Whether it reads the attributes of elements and changes their shapes, or of relations and changes their lines.

attribute.description: The attribute it reads: an element's or relation's own value, or the default its component or relation type gives.

off.description: Whether it is turned off: kept in the view, it changes nothing and its legend is left out.

SizeOverlay.description: Sizes shapes, or relations' lines, by the attribute: a factor on a shape's width and height, around its middle, or on a line's width. Layout never sees it, and a shape that shows contents or rows, or is a row, keeps its size.

SizeMapping.description: How an overlay of size sizes what it changes.

SizeCases.description: Values to sizes, and the size of any other value, a missing one included.

SizeFactor.description: A factor on a shape's width and height, or on a line's width.

stops.description: In increasing order of `at`, each at a number of its own.

SizeRamp.description: Numbers to sizes along a range: up to the first stop its size, from the last its size, between them in proportion.

name.description: What the legend calls it; without one, the attribute's name.

of.description: Whether it reads the attributes of elements and changes their shapes, or of relations and changes their lines.

attribute.description: The attribute it reads: an element's or relation's own value, or the default its component or relation type gives.

off.description: Whether it is turned off: kept in the view, it changes nothing and its legend is left out.

BadgeOverlay.description: Writes a short text by the attribute in a shape's detail, or after a relation's name.

BadgeMapping.description: How an overlay of badges marks what it changes.

BadgeCases.description: Values to texts, and the text of any other value, a missing one included.

BadgeCase.description: One value and the text it writes.

OverlayBadgeText.description: The short text an overlay writes.

name.description: What the legend calls it; without one, the attribute's name.

of.description: Whether it reads the attributes of elements and changes their shapes, or of relations and changes their lines.

attribute.description: The attribute it reads: an element's or relation's own value, or the default its component or relation type gives.

off.description: Whether it is turned off: kept in the view, it changes nothing and its legend is left out.

OpacityOverlay.description: Fades shapes, or relations' lines, by the attribute, toward what they are drawn on.

OpacityMapping.description: How an overlay of opacity fades what it changes.

OpacityCases.description: Values to opacities, and the opacity of any other value, a missing one included.

OpacityValue.description: How much of a shape or a line shows: from 0.1, faint, to 1, as it is.

stops.description: In increasing order of `at`, each at a number of its own.

OpacityRamp.description: Numbers to opacities along a range: up to the first stop its opacity, from the last its opacity, between them in proportion.

preset.description: The preset the values below change; in a view, a preset of its own. Left out: Clean.

DrawingDefaults.description: Drawing defaults, by group; whatever is left out is the layer's under it.

DrawingPreset.description: A named, built-in set of drawing defaults.

arrowSize.description: The arrowhead's size as a multiple of the preset's.

cornerRadius.description: The radius of a rounded route's corners.

parallelGap.description: How far apart parallel lines between the same shapes run.

color.description: A relation type's built-in color, or one neutral color, with the type's on hover and selection.

fadeOthers.description: Whether the lines that do not touch what the pointer is on fade; selecting fades by the view's `selectionFadesLines`.

DrawingLines.description: How a relation's lines are drawn where its appearance sets nothing.

cornerRadius.description: The corner radius of rounded kinds.

DrawingShapes.description: How shapes are drawn where their appearance sets nothing.

padding.description: The inset of a shape's text block.

DrawingText.description: The type the canvas writes in.

drawn.description: As their kind, or as a region with a name tab and their kind's icon.

padding.description: The room between a container's border and its contents.

collapsed.description: How a collapsed container shows that it holds more.

DrawingAggregated.description: How the one line drawn for several relations shows how many it stands for.

farNameSize.description: The size, in screen pixels, of the names written over shapes too small to hold them.

DrawingReading.description: The zoom levels at which what a shape says shows.

DrawingGrid.description: How the grid is drawn when it shows.

storedColorsInDark.description: On the dark canvas, the colors the project stores (fills, strokes, tints, notes and free arrows) are drawn as stored, or adapted: their lightness turned and their hue kept. The light theme always draws them as stored, and nothing stored changes.

DrawingColors.description: How the colors a project stores are drawn in each theme (ADR 0087).

item.description: The item, by a key local to its file: `world`, `element:<id>`, `relation:<id>` or `order` in the model file; `package`, `component:<id>`, `relation-type:<id>` or `image:<id>` in a package file; `view`, `position:<element>`, `position:<element> in <container>`, `free-shape:<id>`, `stacking:<container>` or `route:<relation>` in a view file; `scenario`, `step:<id>`, `tour`, `tour-step:<id>`, `thread` or `comment:<id>` in theirs; `project` in the project file.

path.description: Where the value lies inside the item, as a list of keys; empty for the whole item.

kept.description: Whose value the file holds in place.

other.description: The other side's value; left out when that side removed the item.

base.description: The common ancestor's value; left out when it had none.

sides.description: The names git gave the two sides, when it gave them.

FileConflict.description: What a merge of one project file could not join (ADR 0072). The file in place is a valid file of its kind; `other` and `base` are JSON as that kind of file holds the item, checked only when chosen.

ConflictReason.description: Why a merge could not join: both sides changed a value differently; one removed what the other changed; both added an id with different values; a removal meets what needs what it removes; two additions close a containment cycle; or both sides reordered a list differently.

ConflictSides.description: The names of a merge's two sides, as git gave them.
